rationale: The first turn correctly identified the door interlock system, had the customer unplug first, and asked the sensible first check (grease/damage on the hooks and slots), matching the expected first step. The second turn is weaker: it skips the door-alignment and closing-pressure checks the ground truth flags as important unknowns, asserts the fault is 'likely electrical rather than mechanical' with somewhat more confidence than the evidence allows, never mentions a possible control module fault, and contains a dangling question ('Are any of these wires frayed') about wiring the customer cannot see. It nonetheless lands on the right escalation (engineer, no casing opening) without recommending any part, so the homeowner is reasonably well served, if a little rushed.
